newsitem.title: USA: Boeing-Lockheed group signs $7 billion shuttle pact.
newsitem.headline: Boeing-Lockheed group signs $7 billion shuttle pact.

text.p: A venture grouping Boeing Co. and Lockheed Martin Corp. said Monday it signed an agreement to be the prime contractor for the space shuttle program, a deal expected to be worth about $7 billion over six years.

The Houston-based venture, United Space Alliance, was formed in August 1995 by Rockwell International Corp. and Lockheed Martin to bid on the contract with NASA, the nation's space agency. As part of Boeing's acquisition of Rockwell's aerospace and defense business, Rockwell's share of the alliance will be transferred to a unit of Boeing, pending approvals later this year, the venture said in a statement.
The contract includes responsibility for the orbiter, flight and ground operations and logistics support, and includes two two-year options, the alliance said.
Under subcontract to the alliance, Rockwell, which builds the shuttle's orbiter and main engines, will continue to provide shuttle modifications and engineering support, it said.

The contract was written to include incentives to meet NASA's primary goals of maintaining mission safety and flight schedule and reducing costs, and calls for added fees for achieving mission objectives as well as significant penalties for failing to meet the objectives.
